Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Two-month history of fatigue, reduced appetite, poor sleep, decreased concentration, low mood and libido, and exertional dyspnea.  
• Past hypothyroidism on thyroxine.  
• No vitals or labs available; physical exam not yet performed.

Working diagnosis  
1. Major depressive disorder / adjustment disorder with depressed mood (highest likelihood per symptom cluster and temporal link to new job).  
2. Sub-optimal thyroid replacement contributing to hypothyroid symptoms (medium likelihood given history).  

Considerations  
• Anemia or nutritional deficiency (iron/B12/folate)  
• Obstructive sleep apnea  
• Primary adrenal insufficiency (low likelihood)

Management plan  
• Arrange in-person GP review for full physical examination.  
• Order baseline blood panel: TSH, free T4, CBC, ferritin, B12, folate, fasting glucose, lipids, renal & liver function, vitamin D.  
• Mental health screening: PHQ-9/GAD-7 at next visit; provide information on counseling services.  
• Review thyroxine adherence and last thyroid function results; adjust dose as indicated.  
• Safety net: patient denies suicidality; advise to seek urgent care if mood worsens or suicidal thoughts emerge.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Major depressive disorder – High likelihood: Meets multiple DSM-5 criteria (low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue, poor concentration, appetite ↓, libido ↓); onset linked to new job stressor.  
2. Sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism – Medium likelihood: Known history; symptoms overlap with under-replacement; requires TSH/free T4 evaluation.  
3. Anemia (iron-deficiency or other) – Medium-Low likelihood: Fatigue and exertional dyspnea with reduced dietary intake; needs CBC and iron studies.

● Internal conflicts: Initial uncertainty regarding change in morning erections; ultimately patient reports no change (not clinically significant).
